NoteDown keeps all notes — open and closed — in one Markdown file, plus
one file of the same format per set of people notes are shared with
(`docs/sync-and-sharing.md`). On the device the files are encrypted and
only NoteDown reads them; an exported file must stay pleasant to read and
edit in any other Markdown editor (Obsidian, a plain text editor), so the
metadata is hidden in one HTML comment per note, which Markdown renderers
don't show.

Implemented in `app/js/core/notes-file.js`, tested in `tests/core.test.mjs`;
`app/sample/notes.md` is a complete example.

## Structure

```markdown
<!-- note id=s01 status=open created=2026-10-13T08:05Z modified=2026-10-13T08:40Z due=2026-10-13 -->
## Weekly groceries
- [x] Oat milk
- [ ] Coffee beans (the Ethiopian ones)

<!-- note id=s13 status=closed created=2026-10-10T09:00Z modified=2026-10-13T07:30Z closed=2026-10-13T07:30Z -->
## Pay the electricity bill
Done by bank transfer, reference number in the banking app.
```

- A note starts at its marker line `<!-- note … -->` and runs until the
  next marker or the end of the file. Its body is plain Markdown and may
  contain any headings, so the marker — not a heading — is the boundary.
- Links to other notes are plain Markdown links to `note:<id>`
  (`[Trip to Lisbon](note:s03)`, `docs/requirements.md` → "Links between
  notes and private copies"); other editors show their text.
- Labels (`#travel`, `#😉`) are plain text in the body; the format has no
  attribute for them (`docs/requirements.md` → "Labels").
- Task states are plain Markdown too: `[ ]` open, `[x]` done, `[/]` in
  progress, `[-]` cancelled (as Obsidian themes write them;
  `docs/requirements.md` → "Task states and progress").
- Counters (`23,5 [-4 -1 +1 +8]`, `docs/requirements.md` → "Counters")
  are plain text in the body too: the app changes only the number, and a
  stopwatch's start time in the brackets.
- Highlights (`==text==`, Obsidian's syntax), star ratings (`★★★☆☆`) and
  tables (GFM) are plain Markdown text as well (`docs/requirements.md` →
  "Creating and editing"); a tap on a star rewrites only the stars.
  Other renderers show a highlight's `==` as text.
- Text before the first marker is the file's preamble (e.g. a title); it
  is kept unchanged.
- When writing, notes are separated by one blank line and the body is
  trimmed; the order of the notes in the file carries no meaning (the
  app sorts).

## Marker attributes

| Attribute | Required | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Stable and unique across all files, as notes move between them (no spaces) |
| `status` | yes | `open`, `closed` or `permanent` (a note of lasting value that can't be closed; an unknown value reads as `open`) |
| `created` | yes | Time in UTC, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ` |
| `modified` | yes | Time (UTC) of the last content change (closing or reopening doesn't count) |
| `due` | no | Date `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `closed` | when closed | Time (UTC) the note was closed |
| `left` | no | Shared files only: identity IDs of members who left the note, comma-separated (see "Leaving a shared note") |
| `deleted` | no | Private file only: time (UTC) the note went into the trash; it is removed for good 30 days later (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Trash") |
| `from` | no | A closed note of done tasks (Clear done tasks): the id of the note they came from, for Back to note (`docs/requirements.md` → "Multi-select") |
| `copyof` | no | A private copy of a shared note: the id of its original |
| `copied` | with `copyof` | The original's `modified` when the copy last took its text (Private copy, Update copy); an original with another `modified` has changed since |
| `color` | no | The note's background color: `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `teal`, `blue`, `purple` or `pink` (`docs/requirements.md` → "Note colors and motifs"); an unknown value reads as none |
| `decor` | no | The note's motif: `dots`, `grid`, `waves`, `leaves`, `stars`, `birthday`, `christmas`, `gifts`, `travel`, `packing`, `camper` or `shopping`; an unknown value reads as none |
| `keep` | no | A note imported from Google Keep: `<creation time in µs>~<file name, percent-encoded>` of the Keep note, so a later import recognises it (`docs/requirements.md` → "Import from Google Keep") |
| `kept` | no | Private file only, with `deleted`: the circle (member IDs joined with `+`, sorted) of the shared file the note was deleted from; it shows under that circle and can be restored for it |

**Times are stored in UTC** (the `Z` suffix), so devices and members of
a shared file in different time zones agree on them; each device shows
them in its own local time ("Today 10:05" in Berlin for `08:05Z`).
`due` is a calendar day without a time zone — due on the 17th is the
17th wherever the device is. A time without `Z` (older files) is read as
the device's local time.

Unknown attributes are ignored when reading. A marker without `id` gets a
new one; a missing `created`/`modified` falls back to the other.

## Moved notes

When sharing moves a note into another file (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md`),
the old file keeps a marker without body, so a concurrent edit follows
the note instead of reappearing here:

```markdown
<!-- note id=s03 moved=2026-10-13T09:00Z -->
```

`moved` is the time of the move (UTC). `to`, when present, names the
note's new file by all its members' identity ids, sorted and joined with
`+` (`<!-- note id=s03 moved=2026-10-13T09:00Z to=lea+sam -->`), so a
concurrent edit follows the note there and nowhere else
(`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Merging"). Markers are written after the
notes and kept (`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Files"). Other editors
don't show them.

## Purged notes

A trash entry from a shared file (`kept`) that is removed for good leaves
a bodyless marker in the private file, written after the moved markers:

```markdown
<!-- note id=s03 purged=2026-10-15T09:00Z -->
```

`purged` is the time it was removed (UTC). A device that finds the note
gone from a shared file doesn't put it into the trash while the marker
is there; it is dropped once every device has synced after it
(`docs/sync-and-sharing.md` → "Trash"). A merge treats it like a delete:
an edit on the other side wins.

## Device names

The private file names the user's devices, one marker each after the
moved markers, so every device of the identity shows the same names
while the server knows none:

```markdown
<!-- device id=Qm9vS2V5SWQxMjM0NTY3OA name=Chrome%20on%20Windows synced=2026-10-15T08:00Z -->
```

`id` is the device ID from the device list (`docs/server-api.md`), `name`
is percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent`), `synced` the start (UTC) of the
device's last complete sync round, updated at most once a day; a device
without a name may have a marker with `synced` only. A device names itself when it
turns on sync or restores; a linked device writes the name the new
device's QR code suggests; removing a device drops its marker. Merging
works per ID: the side that changed a name wins, a removal stays, the
later `synced` is kept. Any
text after a device marker is dropped, like after a moved marker.

## Leaving a shared note

A member can't write the file of the remaining members (it isn't one of
them), so leaving only marks the note in the shared file:

```markdown
<!-- note id=s11 status=open created=2026-10-12T10:00Z modified=2026-10-13T08:00Z left=VG9tSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NTY -->
```

The leaver's devices hide the note at once. The first device of a
remaining member that syncs the file moves the note into the file of the
members without everyone in `left` (created on first use, like sharing;
with one member left it becomes that member's private note) and drops
`left`; the old file keeps a moved marker as usual. Merging takes the
union of both sides' `left`. Decided 2026-10-14 over a marker the leaver
writes elsewhere: the note stays readable for the others until one of
them moves it, which is the leaver's choice anyway.

## Members

A shared file names its members with their own display names, one
marker each after the moved markers, so a member who isn't a contact of
everyone still shows by name:

```markdown
<!-- member id=U2FtSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NTY name=Sam -->
```

Each member's devices write only their own marker (the user's display
name, percent-encoded) and keep it current; merging works per ID like
device names. A contact keeps the name the user gave them; a member who
isn't a contact shows with this name in a neutral color (decided
2026-10-14 over "Unknown").

## Contacts

The private file also holds the user's contacts, one marker each after
the device markers, so every device of the identity has the same
contacts and names while the server only knows pairs of identity IDs
(`docs/server-api.md` → "Contacts and invitations"):

```markdown
<!-- contact id=TGVhSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NQ name=Lea color=2 -->
<!-- contact id=VG9tSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NTY name=Tom color=4 pending=2026-10-14T09:00Z verified=2026-10-14T09:00Z -->
<!-- contact id=U2FtSWRlbnRpdHkxMjM0NTY name=Sam color=5 server=https%3A%2F%2Fnotes.example.org%2Fapi -->
```

`id` is the contact's identity ID, `name` the name the user gave the
contact (percent-encoded; the contact's own display name is the
suggestion), `color` the avatar color slot 1–6. `server` is the contact's
home server (the API address, percent-encoded; absent = the default
server, the app's configured API address). `pending` marks a
request this user sent that the other side hasn't confirmed yet (the
time it was sent, UTC); it is dropped once the server lists the pair.
`verified` is the time the user verified the contact (UTC; backlog #4):
by scanning their code or comparing the safety code; absent = not
verified, which is also how contacts written before it read.
Merging works per ID like device names: the side that changed a contact
wins, a removal stays. Any text after a contact marker is dropped.

## News

The private file remembers what the user did with the server owner's
news posts (`docs/requirements.md` → "News from the server's owner"), one
marker each after the contact markers, so the user's devices agree on
which posts are seen, closed or deleted while the server learns nothing
about it:

```markdown
<!-- news id=Nm9vUG9zdElkMTIzNDU2 seen=2026-10-15T08:30:00.000Z -->
<!-- news id=QmFyUG9zdElkMTIzNDU2 seen=2026-10-14T10:00:00.000Z status=archived -->
```

`id` is the post's ID, `seen` the post's `modified` time when the user
last saw it, as the server sent it (UTC with milliseconds, compared
as text). `status` is `archived` (closed into the archive) or
`deleted`; absent = open. A post whose `modified` differs from `seen`
was edited since: it shows as open and updated, whatever the status was.
A post without a marker is new. Markers of posts that are no longer in
the feed are dropped after each fetch. Merging works per ID like device
names. Any text after a news marker is dropped.

## Custom order

A file can hold one order marker, after the device, contact and news markers: the note ids
of a custom order, first to last (backlog #24):

```markdown
<!-- order modified=2026-10-14T09:00Z ids=s04,~Home,s01,s07 -->
```

In the private file it is the user's own **Custom** order: ids from any
of the user's files (ids are unique across files), so shared notes can be
ordered without the other members seeing it. In a shared file it is the
circle's **Shared order** (backlog #25), listing that file's notes and
set by any member. `modified` is the time of
the last change (UTC); without `ids` the order is empty. An entry
starting with `~` is a **section** divider, the rest is its title
URI-encoded (`~Home%20%26%20garden`): it groups the notes after it up to
the next section and is kept as is. Ids of notes
that no longer exist are dropped on the next save. Merging takes the list
the changed side wrote, the newer one when both changed it. Other editors
don't show the marker; any text after it is dropped, like after a moved
marker.
